chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the man prepares his shroud, he is rewarded every time he looks at it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for preparing one's shroud in advance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the spiritual benefit of proactive preparation for death, linking the physical act of readying one's shroud with continuous spiritual reward. The repeated contemplation of the shroud serves as a tangible memento mori, fostering a state of readiness and humility before the Hereafter. This practice aligns with the broader Islamic emphasis on remembering death to purify the soul and accelerate spiritual growth.
